note: Night places that do not expire — a qawwali, a fort lit up, jazz, comedy, cocktail bars, a night bazaar and late-night food. Researched, not visited: every record says so. Programmes change nightly, so the link goes to the venue's own page.

items.title: Thursday qawwali at Nizamuddin
items.area: Hazrat Nizamuddin Dargah, through the lanes of Nizamuddin Basti
items.hoursNote: Thursday evenings, from after the sunset prayer for two or three hours
items.why: Every Thursday after the sunset prayer, qawwals sit in the marble courtyard of the fourteenth-century Sufi shrine and sing, as they have for seven hundred years, with the crowd pressed in around them among the rose petals and incense. Walk in through the narrow lanes of the basti past the kebab stalls, leave your shoes at the stand, and cover your head. Arrive before sunset to get a place. It is free and it is the most moving night in Delhi.

items.title: Jai Hind at the Red Fort
items.area: Red Fort, Netaji Subhash Marg, Old Delhi
items.priceNote: A separate evening ticket; book online
items.hoursNote: Tuesday to Sunday after dark: a Hindi show and then an English one — about 7 and 8:30pm in autumn, earlier in winter
items.why: The Mughal fort after dark, when the walls and pavilions are lit and projected on for an hour-long show of Delhi's history, from Shah Jahan to 1947 and the flag raised here on Independence Day. There is a Hindi show and then an English one. The fort is shut on Mondays. Eat in Chandni Chowk first, across the road.

items.title: India Habitat Centre
items.area: Lodhi Road, next to Lodhi Garden
items.hoursNote: Concerts, films, talks and plays most evenings — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: The best free evening in South Delhi: a red-brick campus by Lodhi Garden that puts on concerts, films, plays and talks almost every night, many of them free. The classical music series is excellent. Check the calendar in the morning, walk Lodhi Garden at dusk, then go in.

items.title: The Piano Man Jazz Club
items.area: B-6 Market, Safdarjung Enclave, opposite Deer Park
items.priceNote: Cover some nights, plus food and drinks
items.hoursFrom: thepianoman.in — open daily, with a night set at about 9pm
items.source: The Piano Man; Time Out Delhi
items.why: Delhi's proper jazz club: a small, dark room in Safdarjung Enclave market, with live music every night and the best Indian and visiting players on a stage you could touch. The night set is at about nine. Book a table on the weekend and listen, because this is a room where people do.

items.title: Happy High
items.priceNote: Tickets from a few hundred rupees
items.hoursNote: A bar on weekdays; the full comedy line-up at weekends — check the listings
items.why: A fifty-odd-seat comedy room up five floors in Shahpur Jat, run by comics rather than promoters, with bare brick walls and the stage close enough to heckle. The weekend shows are where Delhi's new stand-ups try their sets. Tickets are cheap. Make an evening of the lanes of Shahpur Jat first.

items.title: Laughter Nation
items.area: Above Lake View Bistro, Hauz Khas Village
items.priceNote: Tickets from a few hundred rupees
items.hoursNote: Shows most evenings — check the listings
items.why: A stand-up room upstairs in Hauz Khas Village, over the lake, with shows most nights from open mics to headliners. It is the easy comedy night if you are already in HKV for a drink.

items.title: Akshara Theatre
items.area: 11-B Baba Kharak Singh Marg, near RML Hospital
items.hoursNote: Plays, comedy and puppetry most weekends — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: A small theatre complex off Connaught Place, built by a family of theatre people in the early 1970s out of brick, stone and courtyards. It puts on plays, comedy, music and puppet shows. The building alone is worth the ticket. Look at the weekend programme.

items.title: Sidecar
items.area: M Block Market, Greater Kailash II
items.hoursNote: Open every evening until late — book at weekends
items.why: The cocktail bar that put Delhi on the world's list: a small upstairs room in GK-2's M Block market that has championed Indian spirits and ingredients, and which ranked eighteenth in Asia in 2023. The menu changes and the bartenders are the reason to sit at the bar. Book on a weekend.

items.title: PCO
items.area: D-4, D Block Market, Vasant Vihar
items.hoursNote: Evenings until late — you need the passcode, sent when you book
items.why: Delhi's first speakeasy, reached through a telephone booth in Vasant Vihar where you dial a code to be let in. Behind it is a dim Prohibition-style bar with good classic cocktails. Book to get the code. It is a bit of theatre, and it works.

items.title: Hauz Khas Village after dark
items.area: Hauz Khas Village, above the lake and the medieval madrasa
items.hoursNote: The bars open from the afternoon and run late; the ruins close at sunset
items.why: A lane of bars, cafés and rooftops built into an old village next to the ruins of a fourteenth-century madrasa and a deer park lake. Go before sunset to walk the ruins and watch the light over the water, then climb to a rooftop for a drink. It is loud and young at weekends. Weeknights are gentler.

items.title: Dilli Haat at night
items.why: An open-air crafts bazaar with stalls from every state, and food counters run by different states cooking their own dishes. It is lit up and busiest in the evening, when the day's heat has gone. Walk the craft stalls, then eat your way round India. INA metro is across the road.

items.title: Karim's
items.area: Gali Kababian, off the south gate of Jama Masjid
items.hoursNote: Open daily until about half past midnight
items.why: The Mughlai kitchen in the lane below Jama Masjid, cooking mutton korma, seekh kebabs and nihari since 1913, by a family that says it descends from the royal cooks. It stays open past midnight, and the lanes around it are the one part of Delhi where food goes on through the night, especially in Ramzan. Come by metro to Jama Masjid, and walk.

items.title: Moolchand paranthas
items.area: Under the Moolchand flyover, Lala Lajpat Rai Marg
items.why: A parantha stall under the Moolchand flyover that has fed South Delhi's night drivers and students for decades: paranthas stuffed with potato, cauliflower or paneer, fried in butter and eaten standing by the car. It is open until half past eleven. Order two, with pickle and curd.
